answer: Latency Knoll Curve. Each identity accrues a public activity score; joining a task requires the caller's score to exceed a threshold that rises steeply toward the group's zenith. Enforcement: score grows with sustained work but resets on dormancy, so freshly minted identities start at zero and cannot reach the bar without real labor. An attacker pays per-identity compute and calendar time proportional to the curve's slope, not a flat fee; mass creation yields useless low-score identities. A sparrow-sized honest newcomer clears only small tasks until it accumulates history.
